name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria
full_name: AICPA 2017 Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy (with Revised Points of Focus, 2022)
notice: Trust services criteria numbers and point of focus names are used for identification only. Criteria text is copyrighted by the AICPA; descriptions and guidance are written by HCG.

sources.title: 2017 Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy (With Revised Points of Focus, 2022), TSP section 100
Trust services criteria list derived from HCG's copy (criterion IDs, groups, point of focus names and scope)
HCG plain-language descriptions and assessment guidance

scoring.summary: Share of in-scope criteria met. SOC 2 has no official score; an auditor's opinion depends on whether controls meet every in-scope criterion.

rules.summary: The common criteria (CC1 to CC9) always apply. Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity and Privacy criteria apply only when that category is in scope.
rules.quote: a complete set of criteria consists of (a) the common criteria and (b) the control activity criteria applicable to the specific trust services category or categories addressed by the engagement

rules.summary: Points of focus guide the assessment but are not requirements; ones that do not fit the entity are marked not applicable without affecting the criterion.
rules.quote: Some points of focus may not be suitable or relevant to the entity or to the engagement to be performed.

rules.summary: The 2022 revisions changed points of focus only; the criteria themselves are unchanged from 2017.
rules.quote: The changes to the points of focus in the 2022 revisions do not, in any way, alter the criteria in the 2017 TSC.

governing_document.title: System Description
sections: Services provided and principal service commitments
Components of the system: infrastructure, software, people, procedures and data
Incidents and significant changes during the period

glossary.definition: System and Organization Controls 2: an independent examination of a service organization's controls against the AICPA trust services criteria.
American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, which publishes the trust services criteria.
Trust services criteria: the AICPA criteria for security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy.
Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission, whose internal control framework the common criteria build on.
Complementary user entity control: a control the service organization's customers must operate for the system's controls to work as described.

display_name: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (2017, revised points of focus 2022)

controls.title: Integrity and Ethical Values
controls.description: The organization sets and enforces expectations for ethical conduct, including a code of conduct, so that commitments to integrity are demonstrated across the entity.
controls.guidance:
Code of conduct: Maintain a written code of conduct covering ethics, acceptable use, and security responsibilities, acknowledged by every employee and contractor at hire and annually.
Tone at the top: Leadership visibly reinforces ethical and security expectations, and violations are addressed consistently regardless of seniority.
Contractor coverage: Extend conduct and integrity expectations to contractors and temporary staff through onboarding terms and agreements.

objectives.text: Sets the Tone at the Top
Evaluates Adherence to Standards of Conduct
Addresses Deviations in a Timely Manner
Considers Contractors and Vendor Employees in Demonstrating Its Commitment

controls.title: Board Oversight
controls.description: Those charged with governance operate independently of management and oversee the development and performance of internal control.
controls.guidance:
Independent oversight: A board, advisory body, or independent owner reviews security program performance on a set cadence.
Oversight of management: Governance reviews management's design and operation of controls rather than relying on management self-reporting.
Security expertise: Governance has access to security expertise, internal or external, sufficient to challenge management.

controls.title: Organizational Structure
controls.description: Management defines reporting lines, authorities, and responsibilities appropriate to the entity's objectives.
controls.guidance:
Defined structure: Maintain an org chart with clear reporting lines covering security roles and responsibilities.
Role definitions: Document responsibilities for control operation in role descriptions or a RACI so ownership of each control is unambiguous.
Authority delegation: Delegate authority commensurate with responsibility and periodically review it as the entity changes.

objectives.text: Considers All Structures of the Entity
Defines, Assigns, and Limits Authorities and Responsibilities
Addresses Specific Requirements When Defining Authorities and Responsibilities
Considers Interactions With External Parties When Establishing Structures, Reporting Lines, Authorities, and Responsibilities
Establishes Structures, Reporting Lines, and Authorities to Support Compliance With Legal and Contractual Privacy Requirements

controls.title: Competence
controls.description: The organization attracts, develops, and retains people with the skills needed to meet its objectives, including security responsibilities.
controls.guidance:
Hiring standards: Screen candidates per policy (background checks where lawful) and verify competence for security-relevant roles.
Training and development: Provide role-appropriate training so personnel can carry out control responsibilities, refreshed on a defined cadence.
Succession: Identify backups for critical security roles to avoid single points of failure.

objectives.text: Considers the Technical Competency of Individuals
Provides Training to Maintain Technical Competencies

controls.title: Accountability
controls.description: Individuals are held accountable for their internal control responsibilities, with incentives and disciplinary processes aligned to them.
controls.guidance:
Performance accountability: Include control and security responsibilities in performance evaluation for relevant roles.
Incentive alignment: Design incentives that avoid rewarding behavior that undermines controls, and apply discipline consistently for violations.
Escalation: Provide a channel to report control failures and misconduct without fear of retaliation.

objectives.text: Enforces Accountability Through Structures, Authorities, and Responsibilities
Establishes Performance Measures, Incentives, and Rewards
Evaluates Performance Measures, Incentives, and Rewards for Ongoing Relevance
Evaluates Performance and Rewards or Disciplines Individuals

controls.title: Information Quality
controls.description: The organization identifies what information its controls depend on and makes sure that information is accurate, complete, timely and fit for purpose.
controls.guidance:
Data quality: Identify the information internal control depends on (logs, reports, metrics) and validate its completeness and accuracy.
Relevant reporting: Produce security reporting (posture, incidents, exceptions) at a frequency that supports timely decisions.
Source reliability: Prefer system-generated evidence over manual assertions for control monitoring.

objectives.text: Captures Internal and External Sources of Data
Uses Information That Is Complete and Accurate

controls.title: Internal Communication
controls.description: Objectives, responsibilities, and expectations for internal control, including security commitments, are communicated internally.
controls.guidance:
Policy communication: Publish security policies where personnel can find them and notify on material changes.
Objectives and responsibilities: Communicate each person's control responsibilities at onboarding and when roles change.
Whistleblower channel: Maintain and publicize a confidential channel for reporting concerns.

objectives.text: Communicates With the Board of Directors
Communicates Information on Reporting Failures, Incidents, Concerns, and Other Matters
Communicates Objectives and Changes to Objectives
Communicates Information to Improve Security Knowledge and Awareness
Communicates Information to Improve Privacy Knowledge and Awareness
Communicates Information About System Operation and Boundaries

controls.title: External Communication
controls.description: The organization communicates with external parties about matters affecting internal control, such as service commitments, incidents, and changes.
controls.guidance:
Customer commitments: Communicate service commitments, system boundaries, and responsibilities to customers (terms, trust page, SLAs).
Incident communication: Define how and when external parties, including customers and regulators, are notified of incidents.
Vendor expectations: Communicate security expectations to vendors and receive their communications, such as breach notices and SOC reports.

objectives.text: Communicates With the Board of Directors
Communicates Objectives Related to Confidentiality and Changes to Those Objectives
Communicates Objectives Related to Privacy and Changes to Those Objectives
Communicates Information About System Operation and Boundaries
Communicates Information on Reporting System Failures, Incidents, Concerns, and Other Matters

controls.title: Objective Setting
controls.description: The organization specifies objectives clearly enough that risks to their achievement can be identified and assessed.
controls.guidance:
Objective clarity: State security, availability, and processing objectives specifically enough to assess risk against them.
Commitment linkage: Trace objectives to customer commitments and legal or contractual obligations.
Tolerance definition: Define risk tolerance so deviations from objectives are recognizable.

objectives.text: Includes Operations and Financial Performance Goals
Forms a Basis for Committing of Resources
Considers the Required Level of Precision
Considers the Required Level of Precision

controls.title: Risk Identification
controls.description: Risks to objectives are identified across the entity and analyzed to determine how they should be managed.
controls.guidance:
Risk register: Maintain a risk register identifying threats to objectives across the entity, systems, and data, with likelihood and impact ratings.
Periodic assessment: Perform the risk assessment on a defined cadence and on significant change.
Treatment decisions: Record how each significant risk is treated: mitigated, accepted, transferred, or avoided, with an owner.

objectives.text: Includes Entity, Subsidiary, Division, Operating Unit, and Functional Levels
Determines How to Respond to Risks
Analyzes Threats and Vulnerabilities From Vendors, Business Partners, and Other Parties
Assesses the Significance of the Risks

controls.title: Fraud Risk
controls.description: The potential for fraud, including unauthorized access and misuse of assets, is considered in assessing risks.
controls.guidance:
Fraud scenarios: Consider fraud explicitly, including unauthorized access, data theft, management override, and misuse of assets.
Incentive review: Assess where incentives and pressures could motivate fraudulent behavior.
Anti-fraud controls: Map fraud risks to the controls that mitigate them, such as segregation of duties and monitoring.

objectives.text: Considers the Risks Related to the Use of IT and Access to Information

controls.title: Change Analysis
controls.description: The organization identifies and assesses changes, internal and external, that could significantly affect internal control.
controls.guidance:
Change identification: Identify internal and external changes (new systems, vendors, regulations, threats, business models) that alter risk.
Assessment refresh: Update the risk assessment when significant changes occur rather than waiting for the annual cycle.
Leadership review: Review the impact of significant changes on internal control with leadership.

objectives.text: Assesses Changes in the External Environment
Assesses Changes in the Business Model
Assesses Changes in Systems and Technology
Assesses Changes in Vendor and Business Partner Relationships
Assesses Changes in Threats and Vulnerabilities

controls.title: Ongoing Evaluations
controls.description: The organization performs ongoing and separate evaluations to confirm that controls are present and functioning.
controls.guidance:
Monitoring program: Perform ongoing monitoring (metrics, alerts, control self-tests) and periodic evaluations (internal audits, assessments) of control effectiveness.
Independent evaluation: Use evaluators independent of control operators where practicable, including third-party assessments.
Baseline understanding: Establish an understood baseline of control design so deviations are detectable.

objectives.text: Considers a Mix of Ongoing and Separate Evaluations
Considers Different Types of Ongoing and Separate Evaluations

controls.title: Deficiency Communication
controls.description: Control deficiencies are evaluated and communicated to those responsible for corrective action, including senior management and governance as appropriate.
controls.guidance:
Deficiency tracking: Record identified deficiencies with severity, owner, and remediation date, and track to closure.
Escalation of findings: Communicate deficiencies to those able to act, escalating significant ones to senior management and governance.
Remediation verification: Verify remediation effectiveness rather than closing on assertion.

controls.title: Control Selection
controls.description: Controls are chosen and designed specifically to bring the risks identified in the risk assessment down to a level management is willing to accept.
controls.guidance:
Risk-linked controls: Select and design control activities that directly address risks in the risk register.
Layered approach: Mix preventive, detective, and corrective controls at entity, process, and technology levels.
Segregation of duties: Segregate incompatible duties, applying compensating monitoring where segregation is impracticable.

objectives.text: Evaluates a Mix of Control Activity Types
Considers at What Level Activities Are Applied

controls.title: Technology Controls
controls.description: General controls over technology are selected and developed to support the achievement of objectives.
controls.guidance:
Technology general controls: Implement general controls over technology: access, change, and operations controls for the infrastructure controls rely on.
Control coverage: Ensure security tooling and infrastructure controls span the full system boundary, including cloud services.
Configuration baselines: Maintain secure configuration baselines for infrastructure supporting control activities.

objectives.text: Determines Dependency Between the Use of Technology in Business Processes and Technology General Controls
Establishes Relevant Technology Infrastructure Control Activities
Establishes Relevant Security Management Process Controls Activities
Establishes Relevant Technology Acquisition, Development, and Maintenance Process Control Activities

controls.title: Policy Deployment
controls.description: Control activities are deployed through policies that establish expectations and procedures that put them into action.
controls.guidance:
Policy-to-procedure: Back each policy with procedures naming who performs the activity, how, and how often.
Competent execution: Assign control activities to competent personnel with the authority to perform them.
Periodic reassessment: Reassess policies, procedures, and control activities on a cadence and after incidents or change.

objectives.text: Establishes Policies and Procedures to Support Deployment of Management’s Directives
Establishes Responsibility and Accountability for Executing Policies and Procedures

controls.title: Logical Access Security
controls.description: Software, network design and system settings work together to keep protected data and systems open only to authorized people and services.
controls.guidance:
Identity lifecycle: Manage identities from provisioning to deprovisioning in an identity store of record covering employees, contractors, and service accounts.
Authentication strength: Enforce strong authentication: MFA for remote, privileged, and sensitive access; strong credential standards elsewhere.
Asset and data boundaries: Inventory protected information assets and define the system boundary the access controls protect.
Encryption of protected assets: Protect information at rest with encryption or equivalent safeguards aligned to its classification.

objectives.text: Identifies and Manages the Inventory of Information Assets
Manages Credentials for Infrastructure and Software
Restricts Access to and Use of Confidential Information for Identified Purposes
Restricts Access to and the Use of Personal Information

controls.title: User Registration
controls.description: New internal and external users are registered and authorized before credentials are issued, and access is removed when no longer appropriate.
controls.guidance:
Provisioning approval: Require documented authorization before credentials are issued, tied to role.
Deprovisioning: Remove access promptly on termination or role change, with a defined SLA and verification.
Access recertification: Recertify user access on a cadence, removing access not reaffirmed by owners.

objectives.text: Creates Access Credentials to Protected Information Assets
Prevents the Use of Credentials When No Longer Valid

controls.title: Access Modification and Removal
controls.description: Access to data and system resources is granted, modified, and revoked based on roles and responsibilities, applying least privilege and segregation of duties.
controls.guidance:
Role-based access: Grant access through roles reflecting least privilege and need-to-know; exceptions are documented and time-bound.
Privileged access management: Control privileged access separately: separate accounts, stronger authentication, session logging, and periodic review.
Segregation enforcement: Enforce segregation of duties in entitlements, with compensating monitoring where technical enforcement is not possible.

objectives.text: Creates or Modifies Access to Protected Information Assets
Removes Access to Protected Information Assets

controls.title: Physical Access
controls.description: Only authorized people can enter data centers, server rooms, media storage and other sensitive places, and that access is withdrawn when it is no longer needed.
controls.guidance:
Facility access: Restrict physical access to facilities and sensitive areas to authorized personnel with badge or equivalent controls.
Visitor management: Log and escort visitors in areas containing protected assets.
Physical access review: Review and revoke physical access rights on the same lifecycle as logical access.

controls.title: Asset Disposal
controls.description: Protected information is removed from assets and media before disposal or repurposing.
controls.guidance:
Sanitization before disposal: Sanitize or destroy media and equipment containing protected information before disposal or reuse, with certificates where third parties perform it.
Decommissioning process: Formally decommission systems: remove data, revoke credentials and certificates, and update inventories.

objectives.text: Removes Data and Software for Disposal

controls.title: External Threat Protection
controls.description: The organization implements measures to protect against threats from sources outside its system boundaries.
controls.guidance:
Perimeter defenses: Defend external boundaries with firewalls, hardened endpoints, and controlled ingress and egress.
Remote access security: Secure remote access via encrypted channels with MFA, avoiding split exposure of internal resources.
External threat monitoring: Monitor external-facing services for attack and abuse, including credential stuffing and scanning.

controls.title: Data in Transit and on Devices
controls.description: The movement of information to and from the system, and its handling on removable media and end-user devices, is restricted and protected.
controls.guidance:
Transmission encryption: Encrypt protected information in transit over public and untrusted networks with current protocols.
Endpoint and media controls: Restrict movement of protected data to removable media and unmanaged endpoints; encrypt and manage what is allowed.
Data loss prevention: Apply controls to detect or block unauthorized exfiltration channels appropriate to risk.

objectives.text: Restricts the Ability to Perform Transmission
Uses Encryption Technologies or Secure Communication Channels to Protect Data

controls.title: Unauthorized Software
controls.description: Controls prevent and detect the introduction of unauthorized or malicious software.
controls.guidance:
Malware defense: Deploy anti-malware or endpoint detection on susceptible systems, kept current and centrally monitored.
Software allowlisting: Control what software can be introduced and executed, through allowlisting, signing, or managed distribution.
Unauthorized software detection: Detect unauthorized software through inventory reconciliation or endpoint telemetry.

objectives.text: Restricts Installation and Modification of Application and Software
Detects Unauthorized Changes to Software and Configuration Parameters
Uses a Defined Change Control Process
Scans Information Assets From Outside the Entity for Malware and Other Unauthorized Software

controls.title: Vulnerability Monitoring
controls.description: The organization monitors its infrastructure and software for vulnerabilities and configuration deviations that could expose the system.
controls.guidance:
Vulnerability scanning: Scan infrastructure and applications for vulnerabilities on a cadence and after significant change, remediating by risk-based SLAs.
Configuration monitoring: Detect deviations from secure configuration baselines.
Threat intelligence: Track new vulnerabilities and threats relevant to the technology stack.

controls.title: Anomaly Detection
controls.description: System components are monitored for anomalies and security events that could indicate malicious acts, natural disasters, or errors.
controls.guidance:
Security monitoring: Collect and analyze security-relevant logs across the boundary; alert on anomalies indicating incidents, errors, or misuse.
Coverage completeness: Ensure monitoring covers critical systems, identity providers, and cloud control planes, not just servers.
Alert triage: Define who reviews alerts, how fast, and how false positives are tuned.

objectives.text: Implements Detection Policies, Procedures, and Tools
Monitors Detection Tools for Effective Operation

controls.title: Event Evaluation
controls.description: Alerts and suspicious activity are triaged to decide whether they are real incidents that put commitments at risk, and confirmed incidents are acted on.
controls.guidance:
Event evaluation: Assess detected events against incident criteria to decide whether objectives were or could be affected.
Severity classification: Classify incidents by impact to drive proportionate response.
Lessons captured: Record evaluation outcomes, including non-incidents, to improve detection.

objectives.text: Communicates and Reviews Detected Security Events
Develops and Implements Procedures to Analyze Security Incidents
Assesses the Impact on Confidential Information
Determines Confidential Information Used or Disclosed
Assesses the Impact on Personal Information
Determines Personal Information Used or Disclosed

controls.title: Incident Response
controls.description: The organization responds to identified security incidents through an established program of containment, remediation, and communication.
controls.guidance:
Incident response program: Operate a documented incident response process: roles, containment, eradication, communication, and legal or regulatory notification.
Response testing: Exercise the plan (tabletops or simulations) at least annually and after material change.
Notification obligations: Map notification duties to customers and regulators with their deadlines, and meet them during response.

objectives.text: Contains and Responds to Security Incidents
Develops and Implements Communication of Security Incidents
Obtains Understanding of Nature of Incident and Determines Containment Strategy
Evaluates the Effectiveness of Incident Response

controls.title: Incident Recovery
controls.description: After an incident, the organization restores affected systems and data, confirms normal operation and puts lessons learned into practice.
controls.guidance:
Recovery execution: Restore affected systems and data to known-good state, verifying integrity before return to service.
Root cause and improvement: Perform post-incident review, fix root causes, and feed changes back into controls and training.
Recovery capability: Maintain and test backups and recovery procedures supporting incident recovery.

objectives.text: Determines Root Cause of the Incident
Implements Changes to Prevent and Detect Recurrences

controls.title: Change Management
controls.description: Changes to infrastructure, data, software, and procedures are authorized, designed, developed, tested, approved, and implemented in a controlled manner.
controls.guidance:
Change process: Authorize, test, and approve changes to infrastructure, software, and configurations before deployment, with records.
Segregated environments: Separate development, test, and production; restrict who can deploy to production.
Emergency changes: Allow expedited emergency changes with retrospective review and approval.
Infrastructure as code: Apply the same change discipline to infrastructure and configuration changes as to application code.

objectives.text: Manages Changes Throughout the System Life Cycle
Identifies Changes in Infrastructure, Data, Software, and Procedures Required to Remediate Incidents
Creates Baseline Configuration of IT Technology
Provides for Changes Necessary in Emergency Situations

controls.title: Risk Mitigation
controls.description: The organization plans for events that could interrupt the business, such as outages or disasters, and puts measures in place to limit their impact.
controls.guidance:
Business disruption risk: Identify disruption scenarios (loss of facility, provider, key personnel, data) and mitigate per business impact.
Resilience planning: Maintain continuity and disaster recovery arrangements aligned to recovery objectives.
Insurance and transfer: Consider risk transfer, including cyber insurance, where mitigation alone is insufficient.

objectives.text: Considers Mitigation of Risks of Business Disruption
Considers the Use of Insurance to Mitigate Financial Impact Risks

controls.title: Vendor Risk Management
controls.description: Vendors and business partners are vetted before onboarding and monitored afterwards, so the risks they introduce stay understood and under control.
controls.guidance:
Vendor inventory and tiering: Maintain a vendor inventory tiered by access to systems and data and criticality to operations.
Pre-engagement diligence: Assess vendor security before engagement, proportionate to tier (SOC reports, questionnaires, certifications).
Contractual requirements: Bind vendors to security, confidentiality, and breach notification obligations in contracts.
Ongoing monitoring: Reassess vendors periodically and on trigger events; track remediation of identified issues.

objectives.text: Establishes Requirements for Vendor and Business Partner Engagements
Assesses Vendor and Business Partner Risks
Assigns Responsibility and Accountability for Managing Vendors and Business Partners
Establishes Communication Protocols for Vendors and Business Partners
Establishes Exception Handling Procedures From Vendors and Business Partners
Assesses Vendor and Business Partner Performance
Implements Procedures for Addressing Issues Identified During Vendor and Business Partner Assessments
Implements Procedures for Terminating Vendor and Business Partner Relationships
Obtains Confidentiality Commitments From Vendors and Business Partners
Assesses Compliance With Confidentiality Commitments of Vendors and Business Partners
Obtains Privacy Commitments From Vendors and Business Partners
Assesses Compliance With Privacy Commitments of Vendors and Business Partners

controls.title: Capacity Management
controls.description: Current processing capacity and usage are monitored and evaluated so that capacity demand can be met and future needs planned.
controls.guidance:
Capacity monitoring: Monitor utilization of compute, storage, and network against thresholds that trigger action before service is degraded.
Demand forecasting: Project future capacity needs from growth trends and planned launches, and provision ahead of demand.
Scaling mechanisms: Use scaling arrangements (auto-scaling, headroom, burst capacity) appropriate to the architecture and availability commitments.

controls.title: Environmental and Recovery Infrastructure
controls.description: Environmental protections, backup processes, and recovery infrastructure are designed, implemented, operated, and maintained to meet availability objectives.
controls.guidance:
Environmental protections: Protect infrastructure against environmental hazards (power loss, fire, water, temperature) directly or through hosting providers' certified controls.
Backup regime: Back up data on a schedule aligned to recovery point objectives, protect backups from tampering, and monitor job success.
Recovery infrastructure: Maintain recovery arrangements (redundancy, failover, restore procedures) sized to recovery time objectives.

objectives.text: Implements and Maintains Environmental Protection Mechanisms
Communicates and Reviews Detected Environmental Threat Events

controls.title: Recovery Testing
controls.description: Recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery are tested to help meet availability objectives.
controls.guidance:
Restore testing: Test restoration from backups on a cadence, verifying data integrity and completeness, not just job completion.
Failover exercises: Exercise failover and recovery procedures for critical services and record results.
Test-driven improvement: Feed recovery test failures and timing misses back into plan and architecture changes.

objectives.text: Tests Integrity and Completeness of Backup Data

controls.title: Confidential Information Identification
controls.description: Information designated as confidential is identified and maintained to meet the entity's confidentiality objectives.
controls.guidance:
Confidentiality identification: Identify and label information subject to confidentiality commitments at ingestion or creation.
Handling requirements: Define handling requirements (access, storage, sharing, retention) per confidentiality classification.
Commitment traceability: Trace confidentiality obligations from contracts and NDAs to the systems and data they cover.

controls.title: Confidential Information Disposal
controls.description: Confidential information is disposed of when the retention purpose ends, in a manner that meets confidentiality objectives.
controls.guidance:
Retention-driven disposal: Dispose of confidential information when retention periods lapse or obligations end, on a schedule rather than ad hoc.
Verifiable destruction: Use destruction methods that prevent reconstruction, with certificates or logs as evidence.
Third-party copies: Ensure vendors and processors destroy or return confidential information at engagement end.

controls.title: Processing Specifications
controls.description: The organization documents what data its services process and how processing should work, and shares that information so the services are used correctly.
controls.guidance:
Data definitions: Document the data processed, its sources, and the specifications the processing must meet.
Specification communication: Make processing specifications available to the personnel and customers who rely on them.
Definition change control: Version and communicate changes to data definitions and processing specifications.

objectives.text: Identifies Functional and Nonfunctional Requirements and Information Specifications
Defines Data Necessary to Support a Product or Service
Defines Information Necessary to Support the Use of a Good or Product

controls.title: Input Completeness and Accuracy
controls.description: System inputs are complete and accurate, and input errors are captured and addressed.
controls.guidance:
Input validation: Validate inputs for completeness, accuracy, and authorization at entry, rejecting or quarantining failures.
Error handling: Capture input errors with enough context to correct and reprocess them.
Source reconciliation: Reconcile received inputs against source counts or control totals where feasible.

objectives.text: Creates and Maintains Records of System Inputs

controls.title: Processing Completeness and Accuracy
controls.description: System processing is complete, accurate, timely, and authorized, with deviations identified and resolved.
controls.guidance:
Processing controls: Enforce completeness and accuracy through the pipeline with control totals, sequence checks, and idempotency safeguards.
Exception management: Detect, log, and resolve processing deviations within defined timeframes.
Authorized processing: Permit processing to run only under authorized schedules, versions, and configurations.

objectives.text: Detects and Corrects Processing or Production Activity Errors

controls.title: Output Delivery
controls.description: System outputs are complete, accurate, distributed only to intended parties, and protected during delivery.
controls.guidance:
Output verification: Verify outputs for completeness and accuracy before release, reconciling against processed inputs.
Distribution control: Deliver outputs only to defined recipients over protected channels.
Output retention: Retain outputs and delivery evidence per policy to support inquiry and rework.

objectives.text: Distributes Output Only to Intended Parties
Creates and Maintains Records of System Output Activities

controls.title: Stored Data Integrity
controls.description: Data stored by the system is protected and maintained completely and accurately for its specified retention period.
controls.guidance:
Storage integrity: Protect stored data against unauthorized alteration with access controls, checksums, or immutability where warranted.
Retention execution: Store data for its specified retention period and dispose of it at expiry.
Archival recovery: Ensure archived data remains retrievable and readable for its retention life.

objectives.text: Creates and Maintains Records of System Storage Activities

controls.title: Privacy Notice
controls.description: Notice is provided to data subjects about the entity's privacy practices, and is updated and communicated when practices change.
controls.guidance:
Notice content: Publish a privacy notice covering what is collected, purposes, disclosures, retention, and data subject rights.
Notice availability: Make the notice available at or before collection and keep it accessible.
Notice maintenance: Review the notice on a cadence and on practice changes; communicate material updates.

objectives.text: Covers Entities and Activities in Notice
Uses Clear Language and Presents a Current Privacy Notice in a Location Easily Found by Data Subjects

controls.title: Choice and Consent
controls.description: Data subjects are informed about choices available to them, and consent for collection, use, retention, disclosure, and disposal is obtained where required.
controls.guidance:
Choice presentation: Present choices about collection and use clearly, without dark patterns, where choices are offered or required.
Consent capture: Capture and store consent with who, when, what version, and scope.
Consent withdrawal: Provide a withdrawal path as easy as the grant, and honor it across systems.

objectives.text: Communicates Consequences of Denying or Withdrawing Consent
Documents and Obtains Consent for New Purposes and Uses
Obtains Explicit Consent for Sensitive Information

controls.title: Collection Limitation
controls.description: Personal information collection is limited to what is consistent with the entity's privacy objectives.
controls.guidance:
Minimal collection: Collect only personal information needed for stated purposes; challenge fields that lack a purpose.
Collection review: Review collection points periodically for scope creep.
Lawful means: Collect by lawful, fair means consistent with the notice.

objectives.text: Limits the Collection of Personal Information
Collects Information by Fair and Lawful Means
Informs Data Subjects When Additional Information Is Acquired

controls.title: Explicit Consent
controls.description: Where explicit consent is required, it is obtained from data subjects before collecting or using their information for the stated purpose.
controls.guidance:
Explicit consent events: Identify processing that requires explicit consent (sensitive categories, jurisdictional rules) and gate it on captured consent.
Consent evidence: Retain evidence of explicit consent linked to the data subject and purpose.
Refusal handling: Define system behavior when explicit consent is refused, avoiding service denial beyond what the refusal requires.

objectives.text: Informs Data Subjects of Consequences of Failure to Provide Consent
Documents Explicit Consent to Retain Information

controls.title: Use Limitation
controls.description: Personal information is used only for the purposes identified in the entity's privacy objectives.
controls.guidance:
Purpose binding: Bind use of personal information to the purposes in the notice; new uses require review and, where needed, fresh consent.
Internal enforcement: Limit internal access and analytics to purpose-consistent uses through controls and review.
Secondary-use review: Route proposed secondary uses (marketing, model training, analytics) through privacy review.

objectives.text: Uses Personal Information for Intended Purposes

controls.title: Retention
controls.description: Personal information is retained only as long as needed to fulfill the stated purposes.
controls.guidance:
Retention schedule: Maintain a retention schedule per data category tied to purpose and legal requirements.
Retention enforcement: Automate retention enforcement where possible; audit manual stores against the schedule.
Legal holds: Suspend disposal under legal hold with a defined release process.

controls.title: Disposal
controls.description: Personal information is securely disposed of when no longer retained.
controls.guidance:
Disposal methods: Dispose of personal information by methods preventing reconstruction across production, backups, and vendor copies.
Disposal verification: Log disposals and verify execution, including derived copies and caches.
Anonymization option: Where data is kept for analytics, anonymize to remove identifiability rather than merely archiving.

objectives.text: Captures, Identifies, and Flags Requests for Deletion
Disposes of, Destroys, and Redacts Personal Information

controls.title: Access
controls.description: Data subjects are able to access their personal information for review and correction.
controls.guidance:
Access requests: Provide a channel for data subjects to request access to their personal information, with identity verification.
Complete responses: Return the personal information held, within required timeframes, in an intelligible format.
Correction handling: Correct inaccurate information on request and propagate corrections to recipients where required.

objectives.text: Permits Data Subjects Access to Their Personal Information
Provides Understandable Personal Information Within Reasonable Time
Informs Data Subjects If Access Is Denied

controls.title: Correction Denials
controls.description: When a request for access or correction is denied, the data subject is informed of the denial and the reason for it.
controls.guidance:
Denial communication: When denying access or correction, inform the data subject of the denial, the reason, and any recourse.
Denial criteria: Apply documented criteria for permissible denials (legal exemptions, others' rights) consistently.
Denial records: Record denials and their justification for accountability.

objectives.text: Permits Data Subjects to Update or Correct Personal Information

controls.title: Disclosure Consent
controls.description: Personal information is disclosed to third parties only with consent where required, and consistent with privacy objectives.
controls.guidance:
Disclosure gating: Disclose personal information to third parties only under a lawful basis and consistent with the notice and consents.
Recipient inventory: Maintain an inventory of recipient categories and the data shared with each.
Transfer safeguards: Apply required safeguards to cross-border transfers.

objectives.text: Communicates Privacy Policies to Third Parties
Discloses Personal Information Only When Appropriate
Discloses Personal Information Only to Appropriate Third Parties
Discloses Information to Third Parties for New Purposes and Uses

controls.title: Authorized Disclosure Records
controls.description: Every authorized release of personal information to another party is logged, and the log is kept complete, accurate and current.
controls.guidance:
Disclosure logging: Record authorized disclosures: recipient, data categories, purpose, and date.
Log completeness: Capture disclosures made through integrations and automated feeds, not just manual releases.
Log retention: Retain disclosure records long enough to support accounting obligations.

objectives.text: Creates and Retains Record of Authorized Disclosures

controls.title: Unauthorized Disclosure Records
controls.description: A record of detected or reported unauthorized disclosures is created and maintained.
controls.guidance:
Unauthorized disclosure capture: Record detected or reported unauthorized disclosures with scope, cause, and affected data subjects.
Intake channels: Accept reports of unauthorized disclosure from personnel, vendors, and data subjects.
Linkage to response: Feed unauthorized disclosure records into incident response and notification decisions.

objectives.text: Creates and Retains Record of Detected or Reported Unauthorized Disclosures

controls.title: Third-Party Commitments
controls.description: Third parties handling personal information are subject to privacy commitments consistent with the entity's, and their compliance is assessed.
controls.guidance:
Processor commitments: Bind processors and third parties to privacy terms consistent with the entity's commitments before sharing data.
Compliance assessment: Assess third-party compliance with privacy commitments on a risk-based cadence.
Remediation follow-through: Track third-party privacy gaps to remediation or exit.

objectives.text: Evaluates Third-Party Compliance With Privacy Commitments
Remediates Misuse of Personal Information by a Third Party
Obtains Commitments to Report Unauthorized Disclosures

controls.title: Third-Party Notification of Breach
controls.description: Contracts require vendors with access to personal information to report any real or suspected breach promptly, and those reports feed the incident response process.
controls.guidance:
Breach notification clauses: Require third parties by contract to notify of actual or suspected unauthorized disclosures within defined timeframes.
Notification intake: Route third-party breach notices to incident response immediately on receipt.
Obligation testing: Verify vendors can meet notification obligations during diligence or review.

objectives.text: Remediates Misuse of Personal Information by a Third Party
Reports Actual or Suspected Unauthorized Disclosures

controls.title: Breach Notification to Data Subjects
controls.description: When personal information is breached, the organization tells affected individuals, regulators and other required parties within the required timeframes.
controls.guidance:
Notification obligations map: Maintain a map of breach notification duties to data subjects, regulators, and partners with triggers and deadlines.
Notification execution: Notify affected data subjects and authorities within required timeframes with required content.
Notification records: Document notifications sent, timing, and content as evidence of compliance.

objectives.text: Provides Notice of Breaches and Incidents

controls.title: Accounting of Disclosures
controls.description: Upon request, data subjects receive an accounting of the disclosures of their personal information.
controls.guidance:
Accounting capability: Be able to produce, per data subject, an accounting of disclosures from the disclosure records.
Request handling: Respond to accounting requests within required timeframes after identity verification.
Format usability: Provide the accounting in an understandable form naming recipients, purposes, and dates.

objectives.text: Identifies Types of Personal Information and Handling Process
Captures, Identifies, and Communicates Requests for Information

controls.title: Data Quality
controls.description: Personal information the organization holds is kept correct, current, complete and limited to what is relevant for its stated purpose.
controls.guidance:
Accuracy maintenance: Maintain personal information accurate, complete, and current for its purposes, with update mechanisms.
Quality checks: Run periodic data quality checks on personal information stores and fix systemic error sources.
Propagation of updates: Propagate corrections and updates to downstream systems and, where required, recipients.

objectives.text: Ensures Accuracy and Completeness of Personal Information

controls.title: Inquiries and Disputes
controls.description: A process exists for receiving, addressing, and resolving privacy-related inquiries, complaints, and disputes, including monitoring of compliance.
controls.guidance:
Inquiry channel: Publish a channel for privacy questions, complaints, and disputes, monitored and staffed.
Resolution process: Track inquiries to resolution within defined timeframes, escalating unresolved disputes.
Compliance monitoring: Monitor complaint patterns and dispute outcomes as inputs to privacy program improvement.

objectives.text: Communicates to Data Subjects or Data Controllers
Documents and Communicates Dispute Resolution and Recourse
Documents and Reports Compliance Review Results
Documents and Reports Instances of Noncompliance
